posts.caption:
I am so glad you found me! Thought it was time I re-introduced myself. 

Hi, I’m Vanessa! Welcome to my corner of the internet! 

I’m a recovering awkward person, bestselling author, lover of behavior research, mom of two, ambivert, social overthinker. I’m here to be aggressively helpful to you.

So lovely to meet you ❤️

#gettoknowme #introduction #reintroduction #contentcreator #factsaboutme

We all want 3 things: to be understood, chosen and loved ❤️

Conversation expert @vvanedwards says great conversations are one of the fastest ways to get there.

Whether it’s with your boss, your partner or someone you’ve just met, deeper conversations can help you skip the small talk and feel genuinely understood.

What’s the best conversation you’ve had recently?

Comment ‘more’ and we’ll DM you this conversation.
Never Ever Say “Nice To Meet You” | @jenniferhudsonshow

Loved this quote by @jennifer.garner on @aspirewithemmagrede 

I know I’ve found the smallest of kind gestures to make the biggest impact.

A thoughtful text. Holding the door. Checking in on someone. Letting someone merge in traffic. Complimenting a stranger. Remembering the little thing someone mentioned weeks ago.

You never really know what someone is carrying, and a tiny gesture that takes you five seconds might be the thing that makes their entire day a little lighter.

Be the reason someone leaves an interaction feeling a little more loved than they did before. 🤍

What’s a small act of kindness someone has done for you that you’ll never forget?

#Kindness #GoodPeople #DailyReminder #PositiveVibes #HumanConnection

Quick question: what do you think successful people do that the rest of us don’t?

The usual guesses are grit, a 5 a.m. alarm, or some genius-level IQ.

What I saw up close was a lot smaller than that, and a lot easier to copy. Three of the patterns are about how they think. Two are about how they treat people, especially the people who can’t do anything for them.

And every one is small enough to try in your very next conversation.

I’ll share the research behind each one. (Including the one that didn’t hold up. Yes, I’ll tell you which.)

The simplest way to keep someone talking might be something you already do without realizing.

Vanessa Van Edwards explains that a slow triple nod can encourage someone to speak 67% longer. It signals that you’re following their pace, listening and giving them the space to continue.

You’lll learn: 
👂 Great listening isn’t only about what you say
🗣️ A slow triple nod can encourage someone to keep talking
🤝 Small signals can make people feel heard and understood
